text: Git branching is a powerful feature that helps developers work on new ideas without disrupting the main codebase. When starting a new task, you create a feature branch—a separate copy of the project where you can experiment freely. Once your work is complete, you merge that branch back into the main branch, often through a pull request. This request lets teammates review your changes, suggest improvements, and ensure everything works well before combining. This version control workflow keeps the project stable, encourages collaboration, and makes it easy to track what changes were made and why. By using branches regularly, teams can develop multiple features simultaneously and avoid messy conflicts.
